answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. Consider a voyage as the anchor of the cost.
